title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: pKa = −log Ka. A smaller pKa means a stronger acid.

en.text: Acids and bases are defined three ways: Arrhenius (H⁺ and OH⁻ in water), Brønsted–Lowry (proton donor and acceptor) and Lewis (electron-pair acceptor and donor). Kw = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ links acidity to pH and pOH. Ka and Kb measure weak acid and base strength; buffers, salt hydrolysis, indicators and titrations all follow from these equilibria.

am.text: አሲድና ቤዝ በሦስት መንገድ ይገለጻሉ። Kw፣ pH፣ Ka እና Kb የአሲድ–ቤዝ ሚዛንን ይገልጻሉ። ባፈር፣ ሃይድሮሊሲስ፣ አመልካችና ቲትሬሽን ከዚህ ይከተላሉ።

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Arrhenius: H⁺ and OH⁻ in water. Brønsted–Lowry: proton transfer. Lewis: electron pairs.
A stronger acid has a weaker conjugate base.
Ka and Kb measure weak acid and base strength; Ka × Kb = Kw.
Buffers: pH = pKa + log([base]/[acid]); highest capacity at pH = pKa.
Salts can be acidic, basic or neutral. Indicators and titrations find unknown concentrations.

screens.title: Key word
defs: pKa = −log Ka. A smaller pKa means a stronger acid.

screens.title: Match each formula to its use
screens.why: One formula for each part of the unit.
screens.clue: Look for the brackets and the logs.

screens.ask: A buffer of 1.0 M HC₂H₃O₂ and 1.0 M C₂H₃O₂⁻ (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵). pH ≈ ___ (2 decimal places)

screens.why: NH₃ (→ NH₄⁺ or NH₂⁻), H₂O (→ H₃O⁺ or OH⁻), HCO₃⁻ (→ H₂CO₃ or CO₃²⁻). The others only accept or only donate.
screens.clue: Each must be able to gain AND lose one H⁺.

items.text: Which is NOT a conjugate acid–base pair?
items.why: They differ by an O atom, not by H⁺.
items.clue: Pairs differ by exactly one H⁺.

items.text: In CN⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCN + OH⁻, the Brønsted–Lowry acid is
items.why: H₂O gives H⁺ and becomes OH⁻.

items.text: In H₃PO₄ + NH₃ ⇌ H₂PO₄⁻ + NH₄⁺, the conjugate acid of NH₃ is
items.why: NH₃ gains H⁺ to become NH₄⁺.

items.text: In BF₃ + F⁻ → BF₄⁻, the Lewis base is
items.why: F⁻ donates a lone pair to the electron-deficient B.
items.clue: Which species has lone pairs to give?

items.title: Classify
items.why: –COOH acids are weak; amines are weak bases; H₂SeO₄ is like H₂SO₄.
items.clue: Compare each with a compound you know.

items.ask: HCl in water gives [H₃O⁺] = 3.0 × 10⁻⁴ M. pH ≈ ___ (2 decimal places)

items.text: Given the reaction: NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺. The bond formed between NH₃ and H⁺ is
items.why: H⁺ has no electrons; NH₃ has a lone pair on N. N donates both electrons of its lone pair to H⁺ (NH₃ = Lewis base, H⁺ = Lewis acid). A shared pair supplied by one atom only is a coordinate (dative) covalent bond. A and C imply each atom gives one electron; D is wrong because no electron transfer to form separate ions occurs.

items.text: The Brønsted–Lowry concept defines an acid as a substance that
opts: A. furnishes proton to a molecule
B. gives hydrogen ion in water.
C. accepts proton from a molecule.
D. produces hydroxide ion in water.
items.ans: A. furnishes proton to a molecule
items.why: Brønsted–Lowry: acid = proton (H⁺) donor; base = proton acceptor. 'Furnishes a proton to a molecule' = donates H⁺ → acid. B is the Arrhenius acid definition (limited to water); C is a Brønsted base; D is an Arrhenius base.

items.text:
In the following reaction, which is the Brønsted–Lowry base?
HC₂O₄⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) → H₃O⁺(aq) + C₂O₄²⁻(aq)
items.why: HC₂O₄⁻ loses H⁺ to become C₂O₄²⁻ → HC₂O₄⁻ is the acid (proton donor). H₂O gains that H⁺ to become H₃O⁺ → H₂O is the base (proton acceptor). Conjugate pairs: HC₂O₄⁻/C₂O₄²⁻ and H₃O⁺/H₂O. A is the conjugate base and C the conjugate acid (products, on the reverse side); D is the acid.

opts: A. There is no transfer of hydrogen ion from the acid or the base.
B. one water molecule acts as a Lewis base and the other water molecule acts as Lewis acid.
C. a proton is transferred from one water molecule to another.
D. an electron is transferred from one water molecule to another.
items.ans: C. a proton is transferred from one water molecule to another.
items.why: H₂O(l) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq). One H₂O donates H⁺ (Brønsted acid) and becomes OH⁻; the other accepts H⁺ (Brønsted base) and becomes H₃O⁺. So the process is proton transfer between two water molecules (Kw = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻] = 1.0×10⁻¹⁴ at 25 °C). A denies the proton transfer; D (electron transfer) describes redox, not autoionization; B is not the standard description (the process is described as Brønsted proton transfer, not a Lewis adduct between two whole water molecules).

items.text: Given the following acid–base reaction: Ag⁺ + 2NH₃ ⇌ [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺, the Lewis base is
items.why: Lewis base = electron-pair donor; Lewis acid = electron-pair acceptor. Each NH₃ donates its N lone pair to Ag⁺, forming coordinate bonds. So NH₃ is the Lewis base and Ag⁺ (electron-deficient metal ion) is the Lewis acid. A is the product (adduct/complex ion); C is the Lewis acid; B wrongly calls both reactants bases.

items.text: What is the pH and [H⁺] of a 0.2 M solution of HCN? (Ka = 4.9×10⁻¹⁰)
items.why: HCN ⇌ H⁺ + CN⁻; at equilibrium [H⁺] = [CN⁻] = x, [HCN] = 0.2 − x ≈ 0.2 (Ka is tiny). Ka = x²/0.2 → x² = 4.9×10⁻¹⁰ × 0.2 = 9.8×10⁻¹¹. x = √(9.8×10⁻¹¹) ≈ 9.9×10⁻⁶ M = [H⁺]. pH = −log(9.9×10⁻⁶) = 6 − 0.996 ≈ 5.0. A and C give Ka as [H⁺]; C and D also give pH 3, which would need [H⁺] = 10⁻³ M.

items.text: A salt is formed from a weak acid (HCN) whose Ka = 4.9×10⁻¹⁰ and a weak base whose Kb = 1.8×10⁻⁵. What would you expect about the solution of the salt formed from HCN and NH₃?
opts: A. The solution can be either acidic or basic at the same time.
B. The solution will be neutral, because the concentration of OH⁻ equals that of H⁺.
C. The solution will be basic, because the concentration of OH⁻ is less than that of H⁺.
D. The solution will be basic, because the concentration of OH⁻ is greater than that of H⁺.
items.ans: D. The solution will be basic, because the concentration of OH⁻ is greater than that of H⁺.
items.why: The salt is NH₄CN: NH₄⁺ hydrolyses to give H⁺, CN⁻ hydrolyses to give OH⁻. Compare Ka(HCN) = 4.9×10⁻¹⁰ with Kb(NH₃) = 1.8×10⁻⁵: Kb > Ka. So CN⁻ (Kb = Kw/Ka ≈ 2.0×10⁻⁵) is a stronger base than NH₄⁺ (Ka = Kw/Kb ≈ 5.6×10⁻¹⁰) is an acid → [OH⁻] > [H⁺], basic. A is impossible; B needs Ka = Kb; C contradicts itself (basic means [OH⁻] > [H⁺]).

items.text: What is the difference between equivalence point and end point in an acid–base titration?
opts: A. At the equivalence point, the pH is always 7 and at the end point there is a color change.
B. At the end point, the pH is always 7 and at the equivalence point there is a color change.
C. Equivalence point is where stoichiometrically equivalent amounts of the analyte and titrant react and end point is where an observable physical change occurs in a titration.
D. Equivalence point is where an observable physical change occurs in a titration.
items.ans: C. Equivalence point is where stoichiometrically equivalent amounts of the analyte and titrant react and end point is where an observable physical change occurs in a titration.
items.why: Equivalence point: moles of H⁺ added/present exactly equal moles of OH⁻ (stoichiometric amounts). End point: where the indicator changes colour (observed); a good indicator makes it very close to the equivalence point. A and B are wrong because the pH at equivalence is 7 only for strong acid–strong base (above 7 for weak acid–strong base, below 7 for weak base–strong acid). D swaps the definitions.

items.text: The number of equivalents per liter of solution is known as
items.why: Normality N = number of equivalents of solute / volume of solution in litres. For acids/bases, equivalents = moles × number of H⁺ or OH⁻ supplied (e.g. 1 M H₂SO₄ = 2 N). Molarity is moles per litre; molality is moles per kg of solvent; mole fraction is a ratio of moles.

items.text: What is a Lewis acid? It is
items.why: Lewis acid = electron-pair acceptor (e.g. BF₃, Ag⁺, H⁺); Lewis base = electron-pair donor (e.g. NH₃, H₂O). A is the Brønsted–Lowry acid; C is the Lewis base; D is the Brønsted–Lowry base.

items.text: Which of the following is a polyprotic acid?
items.why: A polyprotic acid has more than one ionizable H per molecule. H₃PO₄ ionizes in three steps: H₃PO₄ ⇌ H⁺ + H₂PO₄⁻ ⇌ H⁺ + HPO₄²⁻ ⇌ H⁺ + PO₄³⁻ (triprotic). HCl, HF and HNO₃ each have only one ionizable H (monoprotic).

items.text: Which of the following does respect a general property of a base?
opts: A. Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity.
B. Aqueous solutions of bases turn blue litmus paper to red.
C. Soluble bases release hydronium ion in aqueous solution.
D. Aqueous solution of bases turns methyl orange in to red.
items.ans: A. Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity.
items.why: Strong bases (e.g. NaOH) ionize completely, giving many mobile ions (Na⁺, OH⁻), so their solutions conduct electricity well. B is wrong: bases turn red litmus blue (acids turn blue litmus red). C is wrong: soluble bases release OH⁻, not H₃O⁺. D is wrong: methyl orange is yellow in basic solution and red in acid.

opts: A. ionic compounds formed by complete replacement of ionizable hydrogen by anions of the acid.
B. ionic compounds that result from the reaction between metal hydroxide and water.
C. ionic compounds that derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid.
D. ionic compounds formed by partial replacement of ionizable hydroxide by metal cations.
items.ans: C. ionic compounds that derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid.
items.why: Acid + base → salt + water, e.g. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. The salt's cation (Na⁺) comes from the base and its anion (Cl⁻) from the acid. A is wrong: ionizable H is replaced by metal (or NH₄⁺) cations, not anions. B describes no salt-forming reaction. D is wrong: hydroxide is not replaced by metal cations.

items.text:
For the reaction shown below, which of the following is a conjugate acid–base pair?
HC₂O₄⁻(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺ + C₂O₄²⁻
items.why: A conjugate pair differs by exactly one H⁺. HC₂O₄⁻ loses H⁺ → C₂O₄²⁻: pair HC₂O₄⁻/C₂O₄²⁻ (acid/conjugate base). The other pair is H₃O⁺/H₂O. A and C pair the two acids or two reactants; B pairs species that differ by more than one proton (and are not related).
